1.title: Identity and Access
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Identity and Access. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Describe directory services in Azure, including Microsoft Entra I D and Microsoft Entra Domain Services. Describe authentication methods in Azure, including single sign-on, multifactor authentication, and passwordless. Describe external identities in Azure. Describe Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Describe Azure role-based access control (R B A C). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Authentication and authorization
1.text: Authentication and authorization. Authentication. Question it answers: Who are you? Proving your identity. Example: Signing in with a password and a code. Authorization. Question it answers: What are you allowed to do? Permissions after sign-in. Example: Read-only access to a resource group. Exam tip: Authentication first, authorization second. Microsoft Entra I D handles sign-in; R B A C decides what you may do with Azure resources.

1.title: Directory services
1.text: Directory services. Microsoft Entra I D is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. It stores users, groups and applications and signs people in to Azure, Microsoft three sixty-five and thousands of other apps. It was called Azure Active Directory (Azure A D); exam questions may still use the old name.

1.title: Directory services, continued
1.text: Directory services. What it is. Microsoft Entra I D: Cloud identity service for sign-in and access to apps. Microsoft Entra Domain Services: Managed domain services in Azure. Provides. Microsoft Entra I D: Single sign-on, M F A, app access, external identities, device registration. Microsoft Entra Domain Services: Domain join, group policy, L D A P (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) and Kerberos or N T L M authentication.

1.title: Directory services, continued
1.text: Directory services. Use it when. Microsoft Entra I D: You need cloud sign-in and app access. Microsoft Entra Domain Services: Legacy apps need traditional domain features and you do not want to run your own domain controllers.

1.title: Directory services, continued
1.text: Directory services. Entra Domain Services gives a managed domain that is compatible with Windows Server Active Directory, so lift-and-shift apps that rely on L D A P, Kerberos or group policy work without you deploying and patching domain controllers. A tenant is a dedicated instance of Microsoft Entra I D for an organization. A subscription trusts one tenant (Module five).

1.title: Single sign-on (SSO)
1.text: Single sign-on. S S O lets a user sign in once and access multiple applications and resources without signing in again, using one set of credentials. It reduces password fatigue and improves security.

1.title: Multifactor authentication (MFA)
1.text: Multifactor authentication. M F A requires two or more kinds of proof (factors). Something you know. Meaning: A secret. Examples: Password, P I N. Something you have. Meaning: A device or token. Examples: Phone with authenticator app, security key. Something you are. Meaning: A biometric. Examples: Fingerprint, face. A stolen password alone is not enough to sign in.

1.title: Passwordless authentication
1.text: Passwordless authentication. Passwordless replaces the password with something stronger and easier. Options in Microsoft Entra I D. Windows Hello for Business (biometric or P I N tied to the device). Microsoft Authenticator app (sign in by approving a notification, with biometric or P I N). fido two security keys (a physical key). Exam tip: Password only is the weakest. M F A adds a second factor. Passwordless removes the password and is both convenient and secure.

1.title: Passwordless authentication, continued
1.text: Passwordless authentication. The figure shows this: From password to M F A to passwordless: a convenience and security ladder.

1.title: External identities
1.text: External identities. External identities let people outside your organization use your apps and resources with their own identity. B to B collaboration (business to business). Invite partners or guests to use your apps, signing in with their own organization or personal account. B to C or customer identities (business to consumer). Let customers sign up and sign in to your consumer apps with social or local accounts. Exam tip: "Partners from another company need access to a Share Point site" to B to B or guest users. "Customers sign in to our public app with their social account" to B to C or customer identity.

1.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
1.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Conditional Access is a policy engine that makes if-then decisions at sign-in. It brings signals together and applies a decision. User or group membership. Block access. Location (country, I P range). Grant access. Device (compliant, managed). Grant but require M F A. Application being accessed. Require a compliant or hybrid-joined device. Sign-in risk. Require a password change or terms of use. Example: "If a user signs in from outside the country, then require M F A." Conditional Access needs a paid Entra I D license (P one or higher).

1.title: Azure role-based access control (RBAC)
1.text: Azure role-based access control (R B A C). Azure R B A C manages who has access to Azure resources, and what they can do with them. You create a role assignment, which has three parts. Security principal. Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity. Role definition. What: a collection of permissions. Scope. Where: management group, subscription, resource group or resource.

1.title: Azure role-based access control (RBAC), continued
1.text: Azure role-based access control (R B A C). Built-in roles (fundamental four). Owner. Full access, including assigning roles to others. Contributor. Create and manage everything, but cannot grant access to others. Reader. View resources only. User Access Administrator. Manage user access to resources, but not the resources themselves.

1.title: Azure role-based access control (RBAC), continued
1.text: Azure role-based access control (R B A C). Permissions are inherited from higher scopes to lower ones (Module five). Role assignments are additive: a user gets the combined permissions of all roles assigned. Apply least privilege: give only the access needed, at the narrowest sensible scope. Exam tip: Owner can assign roles; Contributor cannot. Reader only views. R B A C controls Azure resources; Entra roles control Entra I D itself.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors has a legacy app that needs L D A P and Kerberos, and it does not want to manage domain controllers. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Microsoft Entra Domain Services. Entra Domain Services provides a managed domain with L D A P, Kerberos and group policy, without domain controllers to run.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user signs in once and can then open several applications without entering credentials again. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Single sign-on. S S O means one sign-in gives access to many applications.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A policy must require M F A only when users sign in from outside the country. Which feature does this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access. Conditional Access applies if-then rules using signals such as location.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator needs to let a developer create and manage virtual machines in a resource group but not grant access to anyone else. Which role fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Contributor. Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles. Owner can also assign roles.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A partner company's employees need access to one of your apps using their own accounts. What should you use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: External identities (B to B guest users). B to B collaboration lets guests sign in with their own identities.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which is an example of passwordless authentication? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A fido two security key or Windows Hello for Business. Passwordless methods replace the password, for example with a security key, Windows Hello or the Authenticator app.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which statement describes authorization? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Determining what a signed-in user is allowed to do. Authorization decides permissions; authentication verifies identity.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the new name of Azure Active Directory? Answer: Microsoft Entra I D. Question two. Name the three M F A factor types. Answer: Something you know, something you have, something you are. Question three. Which Azure R B A C role can assign roles to others? Answer: Owner (and User Access Administrator).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the three parts of a role assignment? Answer: Security principal, role definition and scope. Question five. What does Entra Domain Services give you without domain controllers? Answer: A managed domain with domain join, group policy, L D A P and Kerberos or N T L M. Question six. Which feature uses signals to allow, block or require M F A? Answer: Conditional Access.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Authentication versus authorization: who you are versus what you may do. Entra I D: cloud identity service (formerly Azure A D): S S O, M F A, app access. Entra Domain Services: managed domain: join, group policy, L D A P, Kerberos; no domain controllers. S S O or M F A or passwordless: one sign-in; two or more factors; no password (Hello, Authenticator, fido two). External identities: B to B guests and B to C customers. Conditional Access: if-then at sign-in using signals (user, location, device, app, risk). R B A C: principal plus role plus scope; Owner, Contributor, Reader, User Access Administrator; inherited and additive. In the next module, we continue the course.
